transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Well, Dr. Smith, my family made me come in. I keep telling them... I keep telling them I’m the reason my friend died. I didn’t call her back when I should have. And, well, I had ugly thoughts sometimes. I just know the Lord is punishing everybody at our church because of me. It's all my fault.
Do you believe that your actions literally caused these events to happen, or do you feel like you are to blame because of how you feel about your choices?

No, it's not just a feeling. I know I literally caused it. When I'm sitting there and the pastor says the prayers, or... or when the choir sings certain lines, I know they are really warning me. They're letting me know that God has marked me, and that the church is suffering because I brought this on us. So, yes, it's real. It's not just me feeling bad about my choices... I really did this to them.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling persistently sad, hopeless, or like you have lost interest in almost all of your usual activities?

Yes. I just... I don't care about anything anymore. I used to love going to choir, and my knitting circle, and playing bingo. I used to walk through Patterson Park all the time. But now... now I just sit in my chair. None of it even feels worth getting dressed for. I just sit there.
Have you ever experienced a period like this before, where you felt this deep sadness and lost interest in your activities for weeks at a time?
No, I haven't. I've never felt anything like this in my whole life. I've always been a pretty steady person, you know? But this... this is different. It's just heavy, all the time.
When you are sitting in your chair for these long periods, are you able to move around or speak if you really try, or does it feel like your body is physically stuck or frozen?

I can move if I really have to, like to go to the bathroom or if the phone rings right next to me. I'm not frozen or stuck like a statue. It's just... I don't want to move. It takes so much effort to even think about getting up, so I just stay there. But my body works fine if I force it.
